note: Extended study of the single-large-prime residual sweep inside ic.pipeline: sizes 20-44 bits, the generic searches, variants and base-shape controls, same binary, sessions, targets and rounds. A structural result, not a leaderboard row: the sweep is a birthday collision search (memory growing like sqrt(r B)). The schema's `ic` band slot carries the sweep at B = 2 (32-bit); the matched rho reference is the session's own rho.negation arm.

rho_reference.band_source: ../../research/ic_sweep_ext_20261028/band/ext-32.json (ic.pipeline residual-sweep:m=2 with a base of 2 abscissae vs rho.negation, 32-bit prime-order curve, 3 sessions)
rho_reference.binary_or_process: ecbench release build of branch lead/ic-sweep-ext-20261028; every arm of a session runs in that session's binary
rho_reference.protocol: each spec's rho.negation reference arm (role reference), run in every session on the same curve, targets and rounds as the candidate arms; prime-order curves (A = 2), so negation is the strongest symmetry available
